In a statement signed by Mallam Bala Nasir, the civil rights group said Governor Usman Ododo’s action has punctured allegations that the ruling party instructed its governors to deny opposition parties access to public facilities for rallies.
The group maintained that the development clears President Bola Ahmed Tinubu of opposition claims that he masterminded a plot to stifle political opposition.
“Governor Usman Ododo is one of the governors closest to the President and would have been the first to implement such an order if it existed,” the statement noted. “By this singular action of the Kogi State Governor, President Tinubu is hereby exonerated from the claims by the opposition that the ruling APC and the President directed governors to deny the opposition venues for their rallies.”
Describing Governor Ododo as an asset to the All Progressives Congress (APC), the FDA urged other governors to emulate his approach, noting that granting venues to opponents does not translate to losing an election, but rather strengthens democratic norms.
The foundation also charged the opposition to reciprocate the governor’s political tolerance by ensuring peaceful campaigns and reining in supporters to prevent lawlessness.
Lauding Ododo as a patriotic leader, the FDA warned politicians against making inflammatory remarks capable of disrupting the peaceful coexistence of Kogi residents. It noted that the governor’s leadership has changed the state’s public image for the better since he assumed office.
Furthermore, the group praised Ododo for his proactive stance on security, acknowledging Kogi’s strategic geographic location and the necessity of sustained investments in public safety. It urged the governor to remain focused on maintaining peace across the state.
